issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares a boolean attribute named 'excellentEnough' in ExcellenceLand, but the solution implements a boolean attribute named 'isExcellent' (with getter isExcellent()). This name mismatch (though same type) can confuse students about the exact attribute name they must declare and the getter they must provide, and may cause tests or instructions that refer to 'excellentEnough' to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the UML/problem statement to name the boolean attribute 'isExcellent' (and document the getter isExcellent()), or (B) rename the solution attribute and getter to 'excellentEnough' (with an appropriate getter name like isExcellentEnough() or getExcellentEnough()) and ensure the constructor parameter order matches the UML/tasks. Update tests/instructions accordingly.
